text.p: British media and leisure firm Granada Group Plc has made an encouraging start to trading in the second half of its financial year, chief executive Charles Allen said on Wednesday.

Allen was commenting after Granada, which has extensive television and hotel interests, announced a 33 percent rise in pre-tax, pre-exceptional profit to 243 million pounds ($397.8 million) in the 26 weeks to the end of March.

Granada reported increased profits in all four of its divisions - Media, Restaurants, Rental and Hotels. Profit before interest and tax from the hotels division increased more than four times to 116.4 million pounds following last year's takeover of the Forte empire.
Granada said its debt reduction programme was ahead of plan following a series of disposals worth over 1.3 billion pounds. Net debt during the period fell 860 million pounds to 2.655 billion pounds.

The company said its media division was well placed for international expansion. Granada is also seeking to boost its position in UK television, announcing this week it was in preliminary offer talks with neighbouring broadcaster Yorkshire-Tyne Tees Television Plc.

"The group is developing into a well-founded international leisure and media business. We will continue to grow these business organically and maximise the benefit of the tremendous assets that the company now has," chairman Gerry Robinson said in a statement, adding he was confident the company would continue to deliver increasing value to shareholders. ($ = 0.610 British Pounds)
